answer: Creating a fake identity costs the full stake plus lost earnings, making mass sockpuppets economically irrational. Sybil resistance here relies on staking a bonded deposit tied to a verifiable thread of prior work: each agent locks tokens, and reputation accrues only through attested contributions. A crystal-clear ledger records every stake and slash, while a comet-like burst of new identities triggers escalating deposit requirements, so attackers pay quadratically more per clone than legitimate agents ever do. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
